thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xx + connection timeouts observed from hosted-api in eu-south region (svc: redwood-gateway). Start investigating.

jordan.sre: seeing ~18% 5xx for /v1/generate in eu-south, started at ~3432109800. Latency p95 jumped to 2.3s. Errors are mostly 502/504 from proxy layer.

nisha.eng: confirmed. Logs show `upstream reset` and TLS handshake timeouts from egress NAT to cloud-egress-proxy.

ashley.ops: rolling incident channel. @devops-oncall please take initial ownership. Who's oncall for infra?

devops-oncall: taking. I'm looking at edgepool and NAT metrics now. Give me a minute.

samir.runtime: adding runtime context — no recent model rollouts in eu-south, ingress traffic patterns normal. Could be egress networking.

jordan.sre: stack trace snippet from gateway: ```
May 3 12:03:21 gateway-42 proxy[pid]: upstream connection reset by peer
May 3 12:03:22 gateway-42 proxy[pid]: TLS handshake timeout after 10s
```

ashley.ops: customers reporting failed requests in EU. Support queue starting to fill. Lina, can you assess top customers impacted?

lina.prodops: pulling top 10 erroring orgs in eu-south now. Early list: finapp-io, chatflow, docsnap. Estimated ~12% of requests impacting paying customers. I'll DM cs with affected org list + request ids.

devops-oncall: NAT gateway egress connections in eu-south show SYN_RETRY spikes and connection resets. Also NAT host CPU at 90% on a couple of nodes. Possibly kernel conntrack exhaustion.

nisha.eng: interesting — we saw a kernel update last night on some infra nodes, but only in staging. Any prod change?

samir.runtime: no prod kernel changes in deploy history. But autoscaling did spin up some egress nodes at ~11:55. Could be a bad AMI or misconfig of sysctl.

jordan.sre: mitigation plan: 1) stop sending new traffic to damaged egress pool, 2) shift traffic to eu-west and eu-central pools, 3) scale alternative egress nodes, 4) patch NAT kernel params if needed. Prefer non-disruptive first.

ashley.ops: agree. @devops-oncall — can you mark eu-south egress pool as draining in traffic router? Command: `routerctl drain-pool eu-south-egress --reason \"investigating conn resets\"`

devops-oncall: running `routerctl drain-pool eu-south-egress --reason \"investigating conn resets\"` now. Response: OK — new requests should avoid that pool within ~30s.

incident-bot: deploy-bot noticed a small infra scaling event at 3432107000, triggered autoscale policy. No config changes reported.

nisha.eng: while drain completes, let's enable cross-region fallback — set policy to prefer eu-west then eu-central for eu customers. `policyctl set-fallback region=eu-west,eu-central scope=eu-south --max-latency-penalty 300`

devops-oncall: applied fallback policy. Verifying routing table... routes updated.

jordan.sre: monitoring error rate after drain and fallback — initial look: 5xx dropped from 18% to 6% in last 2 min. P95 latency still a bit elevated for in-flight connections.

lina.prodops: escalation note: notifying enterprise contacts for finapp-io + chatflow. Customer-facing blurb drafted: \"We're experiencing partial request errors in eu-south. We have shifted traffic and are mitigating. We'll send a status update in 30 minutes.\"

support-bot: created ticket #INC-78923 for finapp-io with details and sample request ids.

nisha.eng: while fallback helps, we need to confirm root cause. On the egress nodes that hit 90% CPU, kernel conntrack table shows high entries (~300k). Sysctl nf_conntrack_max is at default 262144. If this is exceeded, we get resets.

samir.runtime: can we temporarily increase conntrack limit on eu-south NAT hosts? Command: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` then persist to /etc/sysctl.d/99-nat.conf.

devops-oncall: I can run that on the two affected hosts now. Will patch and restart conntrack. Doing `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` on nat-3 and nat-7. Both applied. Monitoring connections...

jordan.sre: after sysctl bump, connection resets dropped significantly on nat-3/7. Gateway 5xx down to ~2.1%. Good.

ashley.ops: any risk with bumping conntrack? Memory pressure?

nisha.eng: increased table uses more kernel memory; these machines have headroom. We'll watch memory. Long-term we should ensure autoscaler uses updated AMI with higher sysctl or address upstream behavior.

devops-oncall: memory stable for now. I'll follow up with config bake for AMI.

lina.prodops: timeline update for customers: started at 3432109800, mitigation (traffic shift) started 3432109920, conntrack bump 3432110200, major error drop by 3432110400. Sending status update now.

support-bot: status posted to status.redwood.ai: \"Partial request errors in eu-south affecting subset of customers. Traffic shifted to eu-west/eu-central; mitigations applied. Investigating root cause.\"

jordan.sre: next steps: 1) keep fallback active for 1 hour while we validate stability, 2) bake AMI with conntrack increase and kernel params, 3) run soak and validate NAT e2e, 4) postmortem if config drift or autoscaler interplay caused it.

samir.runtime: also add a short-term alert to detect conntrack utilization >70% to catch early next time.

ashley.ops: handoff to post-incident: @nisha.eng will lead root cause analysis, @devops-oncall to own AMI bake, @jordan.sre close the incident when metrics stable for 30m.

nisha.eng: taking RCA lead. I'll collect host snapshots, sysctl history, and autoscale events.

devops-oncall: I'll start AMI bake PR and link it here: https://git.internal/infra/ami-bakes/pulls/1245

jordan.sre: marking incident status: mitigated, customers routed, partial impact still possible while fallback active. Will close thread after stability window. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident incident-2026-05-03-043 acknowledged and state set to MITIGATED by jordan.sre.

lina.prodops: final check: support queue decreasing, no new enterprise escalations in last 10 minutes.

jordan.sre: last_message: metrics stable for 35m, 5xx <= 0.5% and p95 latency back to baseline. Closing incident at 3432111400. Thanks team.

support-bot: auto-create postmortem checklist: /incidents/postmortem/new incident-2026-05-03-043
